thread.title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks Climb As Tech Sector Hits 17-year High

author: morningstar.com
title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks Climb As Tech Sector Hits 17-year High
text:
By Carla Mozee, MarketWatch
European stocks advanced Tuesday, with tech shares bolstered by gains for their Wall Street counterparts, but travel and leisure shares slumped after downbeat comments about the industry at a time that oil prices have stepped higher.
Global stock markets, for now, have largely pushed concerns for trade tensions aside.
How markets are performing
The Stoxx Europe 600 Index rose 0.2% to 388.83, topped by gains for the tech and basic materials sectors. But the consumer services group, which includes travel and leisure shares, fared the worst. On Monday, the benchmark rose 0.3% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-ma-cheer-replaces-political-fears-2018-06-04) and marked its best finish in a week.
Germany's DAX 30 index climbed 0.7% to 12,842.94, and France's CAC 40 index was up 0.4% at 5,494.88.
Spain's IBEX 35 picked up 0.3% at 9,775.60, as a new government took over in Madrid. Italy's FTSE MIB index was up 0.5% to 22,111.70.
But in London, the FTSE 100 fell 0.5% to 7,704.56, under more pressure as the pound climbed after the U.K.'s services-sector PMI exceeded expectations.
The euro bought $1.1695, little changed from $1.1699 late Monday in New York.
See:Why a bet against the dollar makes sense as trade-war fears fester (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-a-bet-against-the-dollar-makes-sense-as-trade-war-fears-fester-2018-06-04)
What's driving markets
European tech shares strengthened following big gains for U.S. tech shares on Monday that left the Nasdaq Composite at its first record close since March 12 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-street-poised-for-higher-open-as-jobs-optimism-outweighs-trade-fears-2018-06-04). Early indications from the U.S. Tuesday showed another tech-fueled advance was in the making (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-edge-higher-with-techs-eyeing-a-new-record-2018-06-05).
Tech stocks were bolstered in part by Apple Inc. (AAPL), whose shares hit a new all-time high on Monday, the first day of the company's WWDC developer conference (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-wwdc-no-immediate-catalysts-to-get-to-1-trillion-market-cap-2018-06-04).
The Stoxx Europe 600 Technology Net Return Index charged up 1.7% on Tuesday to hit a 17-year high, FactSet data showed.
But shares of European travel stocks suffered, pushing the Stoxx Europe 600 Travel & Leisure down by 0.6%. Budget carrier easyJet PLC was hit with a ratings downgrade while Bernstein Research flagged current risks for buying airline shares.
"Rising fuel prices are making earnings growth challenging, and while the demand continues to be strong, we worry that capacity growth will limit airlines' abilities to maintain margins," said analyst Daniel Roeska in a research note.
What strategists are saying
"Despite threats and recriminations from China and other global leaders, investors are actively choosing to ignore the trade tariff tensions, with global equity markets rising," said Rebecca O'Keeffe, head of investment at Interactive Investors.
"The G-7 meeting...is now expected to be the main showdown for the issue, with investors hoping that the U.S. administration will backtrack on their current stance -- but they might be disappointed," she said.
Read:Death knell for the G-7 may be at hand after hostile reaction to Trump tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/death-knell-for-the-g-7-may-be-at-hand-after-hostile-reaction-to-trump-tariffs-2018-06-04)
Stock movers
Semiconductor stocks were among top performers Tuesday, with ASM International NV (ASMIY) climbing 5% and AMS AG (AMS.EB) rising 4.6%. STMicroelectronics NV (STM) picked up 3.3%.
Airline shares lost ground, with easyJet (EZJ.LN) down 1.4% even after a ratings upgrade to hold from sell at Liberum. Air France-KLM (AF.FR) fell 3.3%, with Bernstein Research saying "problems are mounting" for the company, including competition in its core domestic market and a running battle with French unions. Shares of British Airways parent International Consolidated Airlines Group SA (IAG.LN) were down 2.5%.
But Ryanair Holdings PLC (RYAAY) shares were up 1.7% despite the company saying Tuesday it cancelled 1,100 flights in May (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ryanair-calls-on-eu-to-prevent-atc-strikes-2018-06-05)and called for "immediate EU Commission action" to prevent more strikes by air-traffic controllers during the busy summer season.
RBS (RBS.LN) (RBS.LN) shares dropped 3.2% to GBP2.71, the price at which the U.K. government late Monday sold shares as it offloaded another 7.7% stake in the lender (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/uk-government-sells-77-rbs-stake-for-251-bln-2018-06-05-34852818). The shares sold for a total of GBP2.51 billion ($3.34 billion). British taxpayers paid on average GBP5 per RBS share during a bailout 10 years ago.
Smurfit Kappa Group PLC shares (SK3.DB)slid 8%, the biggest decliner on the Stoxx 600, as a Wednesday deadline approaches for International Paper Co. (IP)to make a new buyout offer or walk away (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/smurfit-kappa-continues-to-reject-approach-from-ip-2018-05-16), an Irish takeover paneled ruled in May. Last month, Smurfit rejected an EUR8.9 billion euro ($10.6 billion) takeover approach from IP.
WPP PLC shares (WPP.LN) (WPP.LN) fell 3.8% after Berenberg cut its rating to sell from hold on the world's largest advertising firm. "Regardless of the reasons for recent management change, WPP's Q1 relative performance versus peers (particularly in North America) showed that all is not well from an operational perspective: we think that this will prove more difficult and costly to fix than consensus expects," said analyst Alastair Reid in a research note.
Economic data
The final May readings on eurozone services activity came in at 53.8 from IHS Markit versus April's print of 53.9. The U.K.'s services sector PMI was 54.0, higher than a FactSet consensus estimate at 53.1, and up from April's reading of 52.8.
